title: OpenAI and Anthropic poach Trump officials as industry fights for Washington’s trust
source_used: Quartz report on Yahoo Finance, citing CNBC (CNBC page blocked)
key_facts: OpenAI and Anthropic have together brought on at least five former Trump administration officials this year.

Anthropic: Chris Liddell, deputy White House chief of staff in Trump's first term, joined its board in February; Sihao Huang, a former White House OSTP senior AI policy advisor, joined in September as head of frontier compute strategy.

OpenAI: Dean Ball (OSTP senior policy advisor in 2025, helped shape America's AI Action Plan) joined in July as head of strategic futures; Thomas Lind (Office of the National Cyber Director) joined last week for cyber and strategic risk; Peter Bowman-Davis (former chief AI officer at HHS) joined in March.
A federal appeals court ruled in September that the Pentagon had properly designated Anthropic a supply-chain risk.
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei has since attended a group lunch with Trump and AI executives and dined separately with Trump in September, according to CNBC.
Both companies are hiring for multiple political engagement roles, according to CNBC.
quote_evidence: OpenAI and Anthropic have collectively brought on at least five former Trump administration officials this year, a push that reflects both companies' efforts to deepen their foothold in Washington as regulatory scrutiny of frontier AI intensifies.

Frontier AI companies are aware that the Trump administration has a lot of levers over their business, from federal procurement and supply-chain designations to export controls and everything in between, and that it's willing to use them.
why_it_matters_hint: AI labs are building ties with an administration that holds levers over procurement and export controls.
